body.statement: For every \(n>4r\), the test \(\phi_{n,\alpha}\) satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}:\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0}P(\phi_{n,\alpha}=1)\le\alpha\). For every \(\beta\in(0,1)\), it also satisfies \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}:\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\ge\rho_n(\alpha,\beta)}P(\phi_{n,\alpha}=1)\ge1-\beta\), where \(\rho_n(\alpha,\beta)=2b_n+q_n(\alpha)+q_n(\beta)=O(n^{-1/2})\) for fixed \(r,B,\varepsilon,\alpha,\beta\).
body.justification: This theorem gives the requested operational boundary diagnostic, a nonasymptotic size guarantee, and a derived attainable separation rate over one exact class.
body.gap: Leung2022ANI gives fixed-population network-HAC inference from one assignment, and FanLengWu2025 gives low-rank-graphon variance inference for a regression-adjusted average direct effect; neither tests whether a Palm exposure-score covariance is zero using repeated assignments.
body.consumer: A platform with two washout-separated waves can decide whether population generalization requires a network-population variance component before reporting its exposure effect.
